- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean or 0.5–1.5 points.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–3% or 0.5–1.5 points.
- Model consistently underestimates sharp upward moves (spikes) in true outcomes; apply “overshoot correction” by adding 2–5 points to forecast after a spike in sentiment or price.
- Model shows persistent downward bias in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — apply “mean reversion” by adding 0.5–1.5 points to forecast if recent history shows upward momentum.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from forecast at day 1–3, consider “lag correction”: forecast for day 2–5 is 0.5–1.0 point lower than day 1; adjust for lagged momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period volatility — apply “late horizon correction”: add 0.5–2.0 points to forecast if sentiment is positive and true outcome shows upward trend in last 5–7 days.
